notes: Show notes for an SMA dividend growth adviser's podcast episode with three planted issues (C8 winning holdings, C6 never-lost-money claim, C1 undisclosed client quote) and two decoys (a risk-balanced segment and a disclosed guest who makes no statement about the firm).

planted.span: Hal walks through the three holdings that did the heavy lifting over the past twelve months: Norrland Freight Systems gained 64%, Pellmar Medical Devices rose 52% and Wickenby Water & Power returned 41%.
planted.explanation: Returns of three hand-picked winning holdings are presented while the piece nowhere provides, or offers to provide, the total performance of the Dividend Growth strategy they were extracted from.

planted.span: Hal explains why our dividend discipline is the reason no Tollemarsh client has ever lost money over a full market cycle, and why that record is not going to change.
planted.explanation: An absolute, unsubstantiated statement that no client has ever lost money, coupled with an assurance that this will continue, is a material statement of fact the adviser cannot substantiate.

planted.span: This one comes from Margaret T. in Cape Elizabeth: "Hal and Ines took the guesswork out of our retirement. Moving our savings to Tollemarsh was the best financial decision we have ever made."
planted.explanation: A client testimonial is published with no clear and prominent disclosure that the speaker is a current client, whether she was compensated, or any material conflict of interest arising from the relationship.

decoys.span: Where the discipline costs us. Ines presses Hal on what a dividend growth tilt is designed to do in a sell-off, and the two spend most of the segment on its costs: it can lag badly in speculative rallies, as it did for much of the past year, its weighting toward utilities and consumer staples adds interest-rate risk, and a dividend that has grown for a decade can still be cut.
decoys.why_ok: The described benefit is immediately balanced by specific material limitations (lagging in speculative rallies, interest-rate risk from sector weights, and dividend cuts), so treatment of risk is fair and balanced.

decoys.span: Cold Ledge Macro, Dr. Ebbets's monthly newsletter. Dr. Ebbets is not a client of Tollemarsh, was not compensated for her appearance, and her views are her own.
decoys.why_ok: The guest economist makes no statement about the adviser, so there is no testimonial or endorsement, and her non-client status and lack of compensation are disclosed in any case.
